rationale: The question asks how people experience a workload and why they act as they do, which interviews and focus groups answer and counts do not. Residents and assessors describe strategic requesting (c1) and late completion from memory (c5), log data show the delay without its reasons (c2), and no study has asked residents, assessors and administrators together (c4). Semi-structured interviews give residents privacy; focus groups with chief residents and administrators capture the view from the middle of the system. Reporting follows COREQ.
alternatives: Survey of all residents and assessors on assessment time (refused: measures time but not reasons or meaning)
Analysis of the app export alone (refused: shows delay, cannot explain it)
Controlled comparison of two targets across rotations (refused: the committee first needs to know what to change, and one programme cannot randomise safely)
whyNotMoreComplex: A mixed design adding a survey would double the research assistant's workload without answering the why question better; the app export already gives the numbers.

decision.statement: Conduct a qualitative study of how residents, assessors, chief residents and administrators experience EPA assessment workload, with interviews and focus groups analysed by reflexive thematic analysis, and report to the competency committee before the June target review.
decision.question: Should the programme study how EPA assessment workload is experienced before revising its assessment targets?

criteria.text: Residents and assessors describe strategic and delayed assessment that log data cannot explain, and no study has examined burden across all roles.
A programme-wide account of why assessments are late already exists for this residency.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board approval for interviews and focus groups
gates.evidence: Approval REB-2026-0412 dated 2026-09-03, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Protected academic half-day time for focus groups
gates.evidence: Program evaluation committee minute PEC-2026-07 (October 2026 to February 2027), supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Analyse the app export only and set targets from timeliness data
Lower the target to eight now and review comment quality after a year
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c2 and c4 from retrieved records and on two approvals supplied by the investigator.

summary: Qualitative study recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met on investigator-supplied approvals.
